_comment: Single source of truth for the render. Every visual is derived from `seed`, so an unchanged config must produce a byte-identical screenshot. If it does not, something is reading an unseeded RNG.

terrain._comment: region_size * vertex_spacing = world units per region. 2 x 2 regions of 1024 verts at 2.0 spacing => a 4096-unit map spanning -2048..2048.

continent._comment: Radial falloff from the map centre makes the landmass an island. The warp noise pushes that radius in and out so the coastline is ragged instead of circular.

plains._comment: Low-amplitude rolling ground covering most of the landmass.

mountains._comment: Ridged noise gated by a low-frequency belt mask. belt_low/high select roughly the top quarter of the belt noise - open them up and mountains swallow the entire map, which is the single easiest way to lose the campaign-map read.

palette._comment: Texture ids match the order of the assets built in terrain_builder. The reference map is arid: tan owns the plains and green is confined to wetter low ground, which is what stops it reading as generic green terrain.

forests._comment: Density mask decides where woods cluster; the height/slope gate then rejects surf and bare peaks. max_height is the treeline and should sit just under where snow starts blending (palette.snow_height - snow_blend), so forests stop before the mountains go white.

cities._comment: Cities are placed by dart throwing with a minimum separation, gated on flat-ish ground clear of the surf and below the hills. max_slope_degrees is deliberately tight - a settlement draped over a hillside reads as scattered rubble from above.

network._comment: Rivers run downhill from high ground; roads are a minimum spanning tree over the cities; borders are the boundary of a nearest-city Voronoi partition. y_offset lifts each ribbon clear of the terrain - drop it to zero and they z-fight into stipple.

debug._comment: Terrain3D debug overlays, for splitting 'the lighting is wrong' from 'the control map is wrong'. One of: none, grey, control, heightmap, colormap, checkered, autoshader. Must be `none` for a golden shot.

water._comment: Colours are graded by reconstructed water depth, so shallow_color is what you see over the beach shelf and deep_color is open sea. extent_multiplier pushes the plane past the terrain so the horizon is water, not the region edge.

lighting._comment: Low sun angle gives the long directional shadows that make ridgelines readable from a high camera.
